rationale: Asserts distributed consensus/cryptographic proof suffices to confer monetary legitimacy — a direct answer (consensus pole) to what grounds legitimate issuance.

Claims state/regulatory permission is unnecessary for legitimate money — the "regulatory permission or its unnecessity" pole of the issuance-legitimacy question; the file's prose says nothing about transaction visibility/surveillance.

Claims private issuance is legitimate when inside the regulatory perimeter (file summary: firms may issue "if they... submit to regulatory oversight") — an answer to what confers issuance legitimacy (regulatory permission pole).

Claims full sovereign reserve backing suffices to legitimize issuance (summary + reserve_backing_sufficiency omega) — the reserve-backing pole of the issuance-legitimacy question; nothing about transaction visibility/surveillance.
Claims legitimacy of digital money issuance rests on state monopoly (summary: "must be state-issued legal tender under central bank control") — a direct answer to what confers issuance legitimacy.

Claims full transaction visibility is required for legitimate CBDC policy operation (summary/commentary tie visibility to policy effectiveness and illicit-finance prevention) — answers the visibility/surveillance slot.
Claims stable character persists across situations — the character-stability pole the causation-locus slot explicitly includes.
Attaches moral accountability to the individual (grounds individual moral responsibility per file prose) — an answer to where accountability/intervention properly attaches.

Asserts person-situation interaction is the irreducible primary causal seat of moral behavior (file summary and FOUNDING_PROBLEM frame it as the answer to the dispositional-vs-situational causation question).
Claims character is real but context-sensitive — a claim about character stability/instability across situations, which the slot definition names as one of this subject's poles.
Asserts external circumstances over stable disposition as the primary causal seat of moral behavior — a direct pole-answer to the causation-locus question.
Claims character is unstable across situations, which the slot definition explicitly names as a pole of the causation-locus subject.

Locates corrective intervention in institutional/situational design rather than the individual — an answer to where accountability/intervention properly attaches (file prose: interventions reshape environments, not character).
Names cryptographic/capture-time provenance as the warrant of trust in an image (replacing expert testimony per the summary), directly answering the truth-warrant-source question.

Grounded empirically_contingent; per the coordination/founding-problem prose, post-hoc forensic verification cannot keep pace at synthetic-media scale, so verification is feasible only at point of capture — a claim about whether/how authenticity can still be verified at scale.
Asserts verification of visual claims is structurally impossible within relevant timeframes/scale — a direct (negative-pole) answer to whether image authenticity can still be verified at scale.

Claims the generation-vs-detection capability gap is permanent — the slot's own "detection gaps" question; file's Ω irreversibility_claim frames it as whether verification capability can be restored, not as a warrant-source or adaptation claim.

Claims indexical traces remain recoverable (empirically_contingent; summary/omega arms_race_winnability tie it to whether detection can keep verifying authenticity at all) — an answer to the can-images-still-be-verified question.

Claims expert analysis is what carries evidentiary authority (conventional grounding; cs_authority_grounding expertise, credentialed institutional certification per prose) — an answer to what warrants trust in an image as evidence.
Claims social consensus (not indexical/capture-time proof) is what grounds trust in images as evidence — a direct answer, at the consensus pole, to the truth-warrant subject-question.
Claims institutions legitimately adapt to synthetic media by openly acknowledging truth determination as social negotiation — an explicit-acknowledgment-regime answer to the adaptation slot.
Claims the Magisterium (apostolic/moral teaching authority, deontologically grounded) as the legitimate interpreter of AI governance norms — a direct answer to who legitimately governs AI.
Asserts a priority ordering of ends — human dignity supersedes efficiency as the criterion AI development must serve — squarely the value-priority subject-question.

Names the end AI must serve (common good, not extraction/profit), an ordering of governing ends per the file's logic rationale ("coordinates dignity with efficiency... serve human flourishing, not merely profit"), not a claim about property-rights standing per se.

Asserts property rights are pre-political natural law "not human construction subject to collective revision" — a direct answer on the standing of property rights against collective/solidaristic claims.
Rejects solidarity demands to subordinate economic freedom as illegitimate coercion — the opposite pole of the same property-vs-collective-claims standing question.

Claims market discipline (contract law, exit, competition) is sufficient governance, i.e. answers who/what legitimately governs AI with "market discipline" rather than democratic, regulatory, or magisterial authority.
Names aggregate welfare/efficiency as the primary end AI development must serve, with ethical constraints demoted to secondary parameters — an answer to the value-priority slot.
Vests governing authority in technical expertise and demonstrated performance rather than democratic or ethical tradition — an answer to who legitimately governs AI.
Asserts animals hold moral standing as rights-bearing individuals — the rights-bearing-individuality pole of the standing-basis question.
Claims property classification/ownership of animals is itself the violation ("all use—however 'humane'—perpetuates victimization") — the inherent-violation pole of the ownership/use question.
Asserts the "no independent standing" pole of the moral-standing question (file: animals are "ontologically subordinate," excluded from moral standing by definition).
Asserts the property-rights-protected pole of the ownership/use question: use is licensed under property norms, sentience claims cannot constrain it (grounding: conventional property-law supremacy).
Asserts sentience generates moral obligation to animals — a sentience-grounded answer to whether/on what basis animals hold moral standing.
Asserts use of animals is permissible under welfare constraint — directly the permissible-under-welfare-constraint pole of the ownership/use slot.
Asserts marriage is indissoluble per apostolic doctrine — an answer (indissoluble-sacrament pole) to what kind of thing the marriage bond is.
Grounds legitimate governance of marriage in church ecclesiastical authority holding the deposit of faith — an answer to who legitimately governs marriage.
Names Brahminical interpretive tradition (administered via civil courts) as the legitimate source of marriage-governing authority — a direct answer to who governs marriage.
Asserts the marriage bond is a community status rather than an individual contract — an answer (at the community-status pole) to what kind of thing the bond is.

Claims the marital norms are embedded in dharma (divinely given/fixed), while its overridden status and empirically_contingent grounding plus the constitutional-era drift gap contest that fixity — an answer to whether the norms are immutable or revisable.
Names Shariat as divinely fixed ("divine_immutability"; prose: "religious text and tradition... fixed text"), answering whether marriage norms are immutable or revisable at the divinely-fixed pole.
Claims qazi/board community adjudication is the authentic governing authority over marriage ("community adjudication rather than secular state courts"), answering who legitimately governs marriage.

Names communal self-determination as what grounds/legitimates marriage authority — a direct answer (communal-adjudication pole) to the who-governs-marriage question, matching the file's summary of communal custom as the authoritative source.

An empirically_contingent claim (per its cs_axiom_grounding and the cultural_preservation_vs_demographic_strategy omega) that endogamy is a necessary cultural-survival strategy — it answers neither who governs marriage, nor what the bond is, nor whether marriage norms are divinely fixed vs revisable.
Ranks individual liberty above communal authority as the legitimate governor of marriage — a direct answer (individual-liberty pole) to who legitimately governs.

Claims the secular state (via religiously neutral civil law) is the legitimate authority over marriage rather than religious/community bodies — the secular-state pole of the authority-source question.
Asserts users' inalienable right to inspect/modify/redistribute source (deontological grounding, file summary lines 82-84) — a direct answer to the normative status of source access.
Asserts proprietary closure is categorically illegitimate/an injustice (summary lines 84-89) — the "categorical injustice of closure" pole named in the source_access_norm slot definition.
Empirical causal claim (grounding: empirically_contingent) that open/transparent development produces higher-quality, more-secure software — an answer to what openness causes.
Asserts openness is justified instrumentally by quality outcomes, not as ethical imperative (grounding: instrumental) — the instrumental pole of how openness/closure is to be judged.

Foundational deontological axiom asserting legitimate proprietary ownership/right to restrict source access — the "legitimate proprietary ownership" pole of the source-access-norm slot (file summary: creators "have the inherent right to restrict access").

Secondary axiom grounded empirically_contingent; the file treats it as the empirical claim that proprietary licensing is needed for creator incentives (cf. omega creator_incentive_empirical_sufficiency), an answer to what closure causes for creator incentives.

Answers how openness/closure is judged: licensing should maximize aggregate welfare (the welfare-aggregating pole of the evaluation-standard question), per the file's summary "track welfare outcomes rather than ideology".

Asserts the judgment standard is context-dependent (open default for infrastructure, proprietary where it demonstrably improves outcomes) — the context-dependent pole of the same evaluation-standard slot, not itself an empirical causal claim.

Axiom claims prior exploration is what legitimates the trade monopoly (Ω 'prior_exploration_as_legitimacy_basis' and summary treat it as the legitimacy basis for acquisition/monopoly) — an answer to the acquisition-legitimation question.

Axiom asserts papal demarcation binds Christian powers (deontological grounding; prose: papal sanction excludes rival Christian powers) — an answer to what papal authority can legitimately do in the territorial order.
Claims papal supremacy over temporal affairs can license conquest — an answer to what papal authority can legitimately do in the territorial order (theological grounding, holdable status per file).

Denies that non-Christian peoples hold sovereign rights constraining acquisition — the negative pole of the indigenous-sovereignty-status subject-question (file prose: indigenous sovereignty "erased from the legal landscape").
Asserts the Council's four components are structurally independent — a direct answer (composite pole) to whether the council is a unified event or a composite.
Claims the unified/composite framing masks component-level asymmetries — matching the slot's "composite of independent components with masked asymmetries" subject exactly.
Claims conciliar changes are organic development in continuity with prior doctrine, not rupture — a direct answer to the continuity/development/rupture question.
Claims the magisterium's preserved teaching office governs the council's ongoing interpretation (enforced via encyclicals and discipline) — answers who controls interpretation.
Claims doctrine can reverse under development — a direct answer to the continuity/development/reversibility/rupture question (file prose: "Can doctrinal positions reverse, or only develop?").

Claims the Council's 'spirit' is the authoritative hermeneutic key authorizing ongoing reform — an answer to who/what governs the council's interpretation (spirit vs papal magisterium, per the file's omega magisterial_authority_over_spirit).
Asserts what doctrinal identity requires (essential to apostolic transmission), directly answering the slot's "what doctrinal identity requires" clause of the continuity/rupture question.

Denies that textual ambiguity encodes a deeper "spirit" licensing reform (file's prose: progressives "operating in ambiguity space and framing it as Council's spirit"), taking the anti-spirit pole on what governs the council's ongoing interpretation.
Claims S&D provisions are permanent structural accommodations, not temporary phase-outs — a direct answer to the S&D-status question (summary lines 87-90, omega s_d_provision_permanence_ambiguity).

Claims development policy space is an equal-status treaty right — one pole of what the framework fundamentally obligates (reference frame equal_status_development_partnership; dual-formulation note contrasts market-access purpose).

Claims technology transfer is a compulsory obligation under the framework — directly answers the tech-transfer-compulsoriness slot (status overridden; omega technology_transfer_enforceability documents the contested enforceability).
Claims the treaty's core commitment is symmetric universal liberalization — one named pole of the primary-purpose slot (summary: "core commitment is symmetric tariff reduction").
Directly answers the S&D status question at the temporary-exception pole ("S&D provisions are temporary exceptions meant to sunset").
Names non-discrimination as the treaty's primary purpose — the non-discrimination pole of the same primary-purpose subject-question.
